I independently reviewed the full original lem:cusp-sides (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex, lines 1024–1225, including cusppr:data and cusppr:rotation-law), the meanings of all source-facing definitions, the proof bodies in the complete local import closure, and the actual compiled theorem/definition trace. SM.cusp_sides_of_continuous_curve in SM.CuspCurve faithfully proves all four source clauses. This review supersedes the incompleteness assessment of the historical checkpoint041 partial report for this source lemma; that report remains an accurate record of the earlier checkpoint.

Domain and raw curve. The theorem quantifies an arbitrary continuous labelled tuple curve on the actual open real interval (-epsilon,epsilon), with epsilon>0, n≥4 and Generic at every nonzero parameter. Its central hypotheses are exactly the actual singleton unordered point-zero support {j−1,j,j+1}, absence of pairwise-remote interior concurrence triples, and exclusion of P_j from the complete closed segment between the two outer vertices. The turn sign-change premise uses the actual determinant sign at opposite real parameters, on some positive local radius. The previously proved local/shrinking equivalence supplies a witness bounded by epsilon. The curve is not required to extend beyond its interval. cuspCurveGerm keeps that same curve and radius and proves the nongeneric-centre field from the nonempty point-zero set; central nongenericity is not an extra theorem input. The returned proof of CuspAt and the subsequent CuspCase proof are conclusions. No derivative, central G1/Generic, central Regular, preassigned crossing relation, simple polygon, empty cusp or unthreadedness premise is added. NeZero n is redundant under the printed n≥4.

Cases, signs and centre. The source vertex and directed-edge conventions are retained on ZMod n. The actual unique collinear support gives distinct central coordinates and nonzero edges. Scalar collinearity and exclusion from the closed outer segment prove exactly one strict-betweenness case. Case A is B=P_(j+1) strictly between A=P_(j−1) and M=P_j, with f=j−1, g=j+1, c1=j, c2=j+1 and Delta=det(edge(j−1),edge(j+1)). Case B is A strictly between M and B, with f=j−2, g=j, c1=j−1, c2=j and Delta=det(edge(j−2),edge j). These are the actual transparent CuspCase/first/last/corner/Delta definitions, not arbitrary data with the desired properties. The modular remoteness proof covers n=4, and the selected Delta is proved nonzero centrally. The incident outgoing edge is a negative scalar multiple of the incoming edge. The central j rotor is consequently negative real, while every non-j turn is a RegularPair; the centre is explicitly proved not Regular.

Clause (i), actual finite-segment test. Both Cramer parameters are identified with actual supporting-line intersection parameters, including the reverse ordered parameter. The distance from the contacting endpoint is the g-parameter in A and one minus the f-parameter in B. Direct determinant calculations give distance=−det(edge(j−1),edge j)/Delta in both cases, with the source minus sign. The distance is zero at the centre and the other parameter is strictly interior. Continuity at nonzero Delta produces a genuine neighbourhood where Delta remains nonzero with its central sign, the distance has absolute value below one, and the other parameter remains interior. On nearby G1 tuples, the already proved two-segment geometry therefore gives IsCrossing iff distance>0 iff turn j=−sign Delta. This proves an actual transverse interior crossing on generic side values, rather than only an intersection of infinite supporting lines.

The actual turn SignChanges witness, combined with chi constancy on each connected generic side, gives opposite nonzero turn signs for independently chosen positive and negative side parameters. The local crossing test extends to any point of either side by proved crossing-support constancy. The source-facing loop-side Bool is defined by the actual crossing at the positive sideBase and is proved to be the unique side on which the newborn crosses. Its complementary side is noncrossing. The crossing and noncrossing iff statements have, respectively, turn j=−sign central Delta and turn j=+sign central Delta. The latter sign is fixed from the centre; the proof does not assume Delta stays nonzero on the entire original interval. CuspSidesData supplies a single positive radius at which Delta itself has this sign at every parameter, including zero. The side conclusions hold on whole connected sides, so restricting them to that radius provides the source's common shrinking for all conclusions.

Clause (i), every other support. Exhaustive endpoint-against-line classification leaves only the two printed potentially critical remote pairs, in both orientations and including modular wraparound at n=4. All four test determinants for any other pair are nonzero centrally and retain their actual chi signs. In A the unused B pair has its unique supporting-line contact at A, outside [M,B]; in B the unused A pair contacts at B, outside [A,M]. The unused determinant is nonzero by a non-j neighbouring turn and the negative edge multiplier. Uniqueness of the line parameters proves actual closed-segment disjointness, which persists by compact-disjointness. CuspCrossingControl only packages these independently proved facts. The resulting theorem compares every unordered support except the newborn at arbitrary independently chosen points on either side. No thread-order invariance is asserted.

Clause (ii), both needle corners. At the other needle corner the actual central determinant is a negative multiple of Delta: in A the factor is t−1 for the strict betweenness parameter t; in B it is −t. Its nonzero sign persists as −sign Delta. The crossing-side turn j has that same sign, so both named needle turns equal turn j on the loop side. On the no-loop side turn j=+sign Delta and the other turn has the opposite sign. Genericity ensures these are nonzero signs. Both source corner orders are respected, and the final field permits independent loop and no-loop parameters. Whole-side constancy is proved from the actual generic connected families, not imposed as a premise.

Clause (iii), the actual oriented arc. The endpoints are the two distinct actual sigma visits of the same newborn support. The source-facing arc data prove they exhaust that crossing's visits and bind gaussWord to the actual gaussCycle mapped by the crossing projection. Actual traversalShift at f moves the cut to zero; numerical-key inequalities then prove the precise closed arc is the terminal f portion, every parameter on f+1, and the initial f+2 portion. The two crossing endpoints are included by weak parameter inequalities. With the established half-open traversal coordinates, the end of the complete middle edge is represented by (f+2,0); it is included because the newborn parameter on f+2 is strictly positive. Thus no endpoint or vertex is lost. The only vertex parameters on the closed arc are f+1 and f+2, exactly c1 and c2 in the printed cases. TraversalEvaluation is the actual affine edge evaluation, and accepted G1 consequences exclude unrelated vertices on these edge portions. The statements cover every cyclic cut.

Threads and the empty implication. The arc is allowed to contain arbitrary other visits. If two visits of another crossing lay in it, their two actual remote edge labels, each among f,f+1,f+2, would force the newborn support. Generic visit-position injectivity also excludes an unrelated visit at either newborn endpoint; hence a thread visit has its actual other visit in the complementary open arc. GaussVisitsAdjacent means either successor equation in the actual complete nodup visit Cycle, with proved membership. Cycle.next descends through rotations and includes last-to-first adjacency. Because gaussWord is exactly the position-preserving crossing-label map and the newborn has precisely the two exhibited visits, this is the source adjacency of its two occurrences, not an additional adjacency assumption about a different word. The finite sorted-cycle argument identifies the successor index as (i+1) modulo cardinality and proves that one complementary open arc has no visits, including the two-visit case. If the empty arc were the long one, a visit in the short arc would force a partner in it, a contradiction. Thus this particular short arc has no other crossing visit. Every middle-edge visit lies in the short arc, so that edge carries no crossing on the loop side. Its label belongs to neither newborn member; exhaustive non-newborn support preservation transfers the absence to any independently chosen point on either entire side. No general cusp emptiness hypothesis is introduced.

Clause (iv), actual signed rotation. rotationNumber is the accepted finite sum of actual principal turns divided by 2*pi, with principalAngle the argument of conjugate(incoming complex vector) times outgoing. The rotor imaginary part equals the directed determinant in the source. Explicit radius/(m+2) points lie in either genuine half interval and approach the centre by continuity alone. At the singular corner the proved negative-real central rotor, together with the actual constant determinant sign on the side, selects the pinned Mathlib argument limits: +pi from positive imaginary part and −pi from negative imaginary part. All non-j turns converge to their valid central RegularPair values. The finite sum explicitly erases j and then adds the singular side limit; it never uses rotation of the singular centre. The accepted integrality and continuity theorem makes rotation constant on each connected generic side. Uniqueness of the sequential limit therefore identifies its value at any chosen side point. Subtracting the independent loop/no-loop formulas cancels the same erased central sum. Their opposite turn signs yield rot(loop)−rot(no)=turn j(loop), with that sign explicitly in {−1,+1}. There is no differentiability, unwrapped argument, extra angle-domain premise or centre rotation assignment.

Elaborated aggregate and evidence. I inspected the complete 305-line compiled cusp-sides-types trace, including the raw theorem, cuspCurveGerm, CuspSidesData, CuspArcData and all source-facing arc, side and word definitions. Its parameters and every structure field agree with the above source reading. I independently recomputed the full raw theorem's 108-entry semantic-dependency hash fc86e8effeeb5b38737a86d14fe2a5191f1eabb2986f88aa886538910940df59 from declaration-audit.json and matched the mapped source row. Candidate audit042 passed with stage_accepted=false, 1946 audited local declarations and 26 mapped rows. I verified receipt/stage-development byte equality, every one of 209 project and 38 frozen-bundle file hashes, the exact 203-module SM inventory, all 185 previous SM files unchanged from checkpoint041, the source and full type-trace hashes, and the exact 74-file import closure recorded below. The 18 new modules match the bytes inspected in the independent preliminary reviews; the 56 inherited files match this reviewer's prior source/body review evidence. The main theorem and printed principal subresults use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. These compilation/hash checks support, but do not replace, the source/type/body comparison. This signs only the original lem:cusp-sides and its clause aliases; it does not certify full def:walls, the main state-sum wall laws, the soft theorem, or the complete stage. Helpers are not additional original claims.

countersignature_20260913.reason: SM.cusp_sides_of_continuous_curve (work/lean/SM/CuspCurve.lean:26-46) takes exactly the printed hypotheses of lem:cusp-sides (sm-1-polygons.tex:1051-1064): n>=4 (hn); a continuous P : Ioo(-eps,eps) -> (ZMod n -> R^2) (hP); Generic = G1 and G2 for t != 0 (hg; Generic.lean:11-19 matches def:generic lines 100-107); at t=0 the sole collinear triple {j-1,j,j+1} (hz: pointZeroTriples (P 0) = {turnSupport j}; ZeroTriples.lean:13-14,39-41, TurnSupports.lean:10), no pairwise-remote interior concurrence (hconc: concurrenceTriples = empty; ZeroTriples.lean:61-67), mu_j outside the closed segment [mu_{j-1},mu_{j+1}] (hout, literal parametrisation r in [0,1]), and tau_j changes sign in the def:germ sense (hchange: exists delta>0, for 0<t<delta, turn(P t) j * turn(P(-t)) j < 0, matching lines 693-694). cuspCurveGerm only repackages these into a WallGerm (WallGerm.lean:13-19), deriving the nongeneric centre from hz, so no hypothesis is added. Conclusion: exists b, CuspCase centre j b with case_unique gives 'exactly one case applies'; CuspCase true = StrictBetween mu_{j-1} mu_{j+1} mu_j (case A), false = StrictBetween mu_j mu_{j-1} mu_{j+1} (case B) (CuspDefinition.lean:12-14, StrictBetween.lean:9-10), and cuspFirst/cuspLast/cuspCorner/cuspDelta (CuspDefinition.lean:16-27) give (f,g)=(j-1,j+1),(c1,c2)=(j,j+1),Delta=det(lambda_{j-1},lambda_{j+1}) in A and (j-2,j),(j-1,j),det(lambda_{j-2},lambda_j) in B, exactly table cusppr:data (lines 1066-1074). CuspSidesData (CuspSides.lean:13-54): (i) delta_neighborhood = Delta nonzero with constant sign on a shrunk radius; side_laws = the newborn pair crosses iff side = loop side iff tau_j = -sgn Delta, and does not cross iff tau_j = +sgn Delta; remote_pair; other_crossings = no other crossing pair changes (all Finset pairs != {f,g}, IsCrossing agrees across any side/parameter). (ii) needle_turns = on the loop side turn c1 = turn c2 = turn j, on the no-loop side turn c1 = -turn c2. (iii) loop_arc : CuspArcData (CuspArcData.lean:21-37): closed_arc characterises the arc between the two newborn visits as {(f,t): t >= t_first} U all of edge f+1 (= the edge from c1 to c2) U {(f+2,t): t <= t_last}, vertices says its only vertices are f+1=c1 and f+2=c2 (traversalVertex i = (i,0), ThreeEdgeArc.lean:67), empty_of_adjacent says GaussVisitsAdjacent (next in the sorted cyclic visit sequence, GaussCyclicGap.lean:25, GaussWord.lean:17-25,84-89, matching def:gauss lines 249-257) implies no visit in the open arc; empty_middle_edge gives, under that adjacency on the loop side, that no crossing on either side contains edge index c1 = f+1, i.e. the c1-c2 edge carries no crossing on either side of the wall. (iv) rotation_jump = rotationNumber(loop) - rotationNumber(no-loop) = (turn loop j : R) with turn in {-1,1}; rotationNumber = (sum principalTurn)/(2 pi) with principalTurn = arg(conj(u) v), whose cos and sign match def:regular lines 386-396 (RotationNumber.lean:10-11, RegularLocus.lean:15-16, RegularPairs.lean:54, EuclideanPlane.lean:55-63). Same domain, same quantifiers, same conclusions; nothing vacuous (the hypotheses are the source's, unchanged). sm15_reworded is false and CHANGES_SINCE_20260909.md does not mention this lemma; the blueprint extract equals source lines 1051-1099, and the accepted Lean statement matches that SM15 text.
stronger_than_source: side_laws, other_crossings, needle_turns, rotation_jump, loop_arc and empty_middle_edge are asserted for every side parameter s,t in the whole germ interval (0,eps), with the two sides' parameters chosen independently, whereas the source states (i)-(iv) only 'after shrinking the parameter interval' (sm-1-polygons.tex:1075); the shrinking survives only in delta_neighborhood for Delta.

CuspArcData.thread_partner (CuspArcData.lean:31-35) asserts that every non-newborn visit inside the open short arc has its partner visit in the complementary open arc; the printed clause (iii) only says the arc 'is allowed to contain other crossing visits' (line 1084-1085). This is a fact from the printed proof (lines 1216-1223), not from the statement.

other_crossings (CuspSides.lean:26-28) quantifies over all Finset pairs and all pairs of side/parameter choices, so it also asserts within-side constancy of every non-newborn crossing pair, not just agreement across the wall.
delta_neighborhood includes the centre t=0 (Delta(0) != 0) and a witness radius delta <= g.radius; the source only says Delta is nonzero with constant sign after shrinking.

Bookkeeping clauses with no printed counterpart: case_unique is stated as a universally quantified uniqueness (the source says 'exactly one case applies', same content); CuspArcData.distinct_visits, same_crossing, visits_exhaust and actual_word are extra structural facts about the two newborn visits and the Gauss word.
